items.name: MOTS-C
items.benefits: Preclinical evidence: administered MOTS-c improved metabolic homeostasis and insulin sensitivity in mouse research, and increased physical performance in young and old mice. The human portion of the exercise study measured the body's own MOTS-c response to exercise; it did not test MOTS-c injections as treatment. Human benefits for weight loss, exercise performance, muscle preservation, or anti-aging remain unestablished in the primary evidence found.

source_statements.excerpt: Anyone with an active cancer diagnosis, since MOTS-c effects on tumor biology are mixed in the literature and clinician sources cited by Innerbody recommend caution.

source_statements.section: Who MOTS-c Is For and Who Should Avoid It

source_statements.section: Who MOTS-c Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: Athletes subject to drug testing under WADA rules, since MOTS-c is prohibited at all times under section S4.4.1.

source_statements.section: MOTS-c Side Effects & Safety
source_statements.excerpt: There is no large human safety database for MOTS-c. The closest published human safety data is for CB4211 , a synthetic MOTS-c analog that completed a Phase 1 trial and was reported as well tolerated. That is similar but not the same molecule, so the read-across is limited.
